subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as Gateway-attested connect metadata, as an explicitly untrusted diagnostic hint, or not exposed to agents yet?
rationale: Agents may use this value for native-only UX, deep links, debugging, or capability decisions, so automation should not choose the trust semantics or carrier shape without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Gateway-attested metadata
options.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime field and document what agents may trust.

options.title: Untrusted diagnostic hint
options.body: Expose a clearly labeled untrusted client hint for debugging only and forbid permission or capability decisions from using it.

options.title: Keep runtime exposure closed
options.body: Limit client identity to Gateway diagnostics until maintainers approve a stronger client-attestation design.

recommendation.title: Gateway-attested metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime field and document what agents may trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the Gateway protocol, client identity, and runtime prompt boundary where the strongest history signal points to steipete.
